Alright, after all those documentation edits I need to make sure the user sees the updated CLI experience. The recent changes to the README and AGENTS files introduced new effort modes (including “ultracode”) and clarified subagent behavior. Those updates should be reflected in the glint CLI’s startup banner and transition messages – the wordmark that prints on launch and the short intro that explains the new features.

The best way to verify that is to actually run glint in its TUI mode and capture what it prints on startup. I’ve been using tmux sessions for this throughout the session: earlier I launched a session named “glint”, sent keys, and captured the pane to retrieve story output. Now I need a clean slate, because the previous session still has lingering state and could interfere with the fresh launch. So I’ll first kill any existing “glint” session, ignoring errors if it doesn’t exist (`tmux kill-session -t glint 2>/dev/null`). A short pause (`sleep 0.5`) will give tmux a moment to clean up.

Next, I’ll start a new detached tmux session with a reasonable terminal size that matches the typical display of the CLI (width 110, height 38). The working directory should be the temporary test directory `/tmp/glint-test` where the earlier story generation happened, but the CLI itself doesn’t depend on any specific files for the intro – it just needs to run. I’ll launch `glint` inside this session, redirecting its stderr to a log file (`/tmp/glint-tui-err.log`) so I can inspect any launch errors later without cluttering the pane output.

I need to give glint a moment to render its wordmark and the introductory text. From previous runs, about 2–3 seconds is enough for the banner to appear. I’ll wait `2.6` seconds, then capture the pane contents, strip empty lines (`grep -v '^\s*$'`), and take the last six lines (`tail -6`). Those should include the wordmark and the first part of the transition message.

To verify the transition continues (e.g., a second paragraph or a prompt), I’ll wait a bit longer – another three seconds – and capture the pane again, this time taking the last four lines (`tail -4`). This second capture should show any additional intro text that appears after the initial banner.

Putting it all together, the command sequence is:
1. `tmux kill-session -t glint 2>/dev/null`
2. `sleep 0.5`
3. `tmux new-session -d -s glint -x 110 -y 38 -c /tmp/glint-test 'glint 2>/tmp/glint-tui-err.log'`
4. `sleep 2.6 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -6`
5. `sleep 3 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -4`

All of this can be wrapped in a single Bash tool call with a clear description (“Final intro check: wordmark and transition”).
